findings.description: The proposed empty password_hash representation introduces a timing oracle through the preserved public password-login endpoint unless its verification path changes explicitly. Current verification rejects an empty hash immediately as InvalidHashError, whereas an unknown account performs an expensive Argon2 dummy verification. An attacker could distinguish passwordless registered addresses from unknown addresses despite identical error responses. The plan specifies the new representation but does not specify the compensating verification behavior or its regression evidence.
evidence: specs/022-modern-auth/plan.md, Phase 1 A: password_hash remains a mandatory string, with "" representing an unset password; the known dummy timing hash must never be assigned.
specs/022-modern-auth/data-model.md, users row and Authority invariants: passwordless accounts use an empty password hash.

backend/app/services/auth_service.py, AuthService._verify_password: InvalidHashError returns False immediately; AuthService.login performs dummy Argon2 verification only when the user lookup returns None.
docs/auth.md, decision 5: password login must not disclose account existence through response wording or verification timing.
specs/022-modern-auth/quickstart.md, Browser journeys: the planned negative evidence does not cover passwordless-versus-unknown password verification cost.
findings.recommendation: Amend the technical plan and validation matrix so unset or invalid password hashes perform comparable dummy Argon2 verification work and then reject unconditionally. Keep the dummy hash outside account persistence and never treat matching its known password as successful authentication. Add a focused deterministic regression check proving unknown and passwordless accounts both invoke the expensive verification path and that every passwordless password attempt fails without issuing a session.
